messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Intel compiler
parts:
Intel released the 2013 edition of its C++ compiler. You can get it from

http://software.intel.com/en-us/non-commercial-software-development

Stan seems to (still) work with it, although it is even worse than g++ in terms of compilation speed and RAM consumption.

You can make a rstan package by doing make install in the rstan/ director with something like this in ~/.R/Makevars

CC=icc
CXX=icpc

CXXFLAGS = -O3 -pipe -mp $(LTO)  #set_by_rstan
R_XTRA_CPPFLAGS =  -I$(R_INCLUDE_DIR) -DNDEBUG  #set_by_rstan

ICC_LIBS=/opt/IntelCPP/lib
LDFLAGS="-L$ICC_LIBS"
SHLIB_CXXLD=icpc

possibly changing ICC_LIBS to wherever you installed it. Benching said rstan package against a clang version with this .R file

stopifnot(require(rstan))
stopifnot(require(parallel))

example(stan_demo)

bench <- function(i) {
  mark <- "elapsed"
  compile <- system.time(fit <- stan_demo(i, chains = 0, iter = 0))[mark]
  execute <- system.time(fit <- stan_demo(i, fit = fit, seed = 12345, refresh = -1))[mark]
  if(length(dim(fit)) == 0) execute <- NA_real_ # failure
  return(c(compile, execute))
}

results <- mclapply(1:length(model_names), mc.cores = 4L, FUN = bench,
                    mc.preschedule = FALSE)

names(results) <- model_names


suggests that Intel might have a slight advantage in computation time.



This is not configuring Eigen to use the Intel Math Library backend and excludes an outlier (schools) that takes more than 1700 seconds for Clang and 2700 seconds for Intel.

If we can get some confirmation on Mac / Windows, we could probably mention the Intel compiler in the manual.

Ben

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Intel compiler
parts:
My guess is that the major gain to be had from using ICC would come from using their BLAS implementation, so it's not shocking to me that we don't see much of a difference here.

Matt

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Intel compiler
parts:
I could do that but

http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/TopicUsingIntelMKL.html

says that Eigen only MKL's operations on double / float / complex. So, I didn't think it would make much difference to test-models.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Intel compiler
parts:
On 11/5/12 7:09 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> I could do that but
>
> http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/TopicUsingIntelMKL.html
>
> says that Eigen only MKL's operations on double / float / complex. So, I didn't think it would make much difference to
> test-models.

This should change over time if we unfold
more of the matrix operations into direct
computations of derivatives. Then all the
ops will be on doubles and those are way
more optimizable than stan::agrad::var.

- Bob
